newsitem.title: UK: Firm sterling pushes quiet UK grain futures down.
newsitem.headline: Firm sterling pushes quiet UK grain futures down.

text.p: A firmer sterling pushed LIFFE grains futures down in subdued trading.
There were some buyers around, but the market appeared to be winding-down for the holiday, one trader said.
Just 84 lots of wheat and 15 lots of barley were traded during the day.
March was most active in wheat, with 47 lots. It last traded 0.60 stg lower, at 97.60 stg, the biggest fall for wheat.
The active month in barley was also March, with 10 lots, which last traded down 0.50 stg at 95.25 stg per tonne.
There were four lots traded in the Amsterdam exchange's wheat contract today. Two were in February, which was down 3 marks to 272 marks per tonne, and two in April, up 3 marks to 280 marks per tonne.
